items.name: HL · Form order → Sheet + alert
items.what: One nine-step Zap: a Google Form order is cleaned (phone, date), priced from the Products sheet, given a delivery fee by area (with a fallback), totalled, saved as a clean row in Orders with the total as a plain number, and emailed to Tolu with the total shown in naira.
steps: 1 · Trigger · Google Forms › New Form Response: Form = the order form from 1.1 Bronze (name, phone, product, quantity, delivery date) with an Area dropdown added.

2 · Action · Formatter by Zapier › Numbers › Format Phone Number (rename step "Clean phone"): Input = [1. Phone]; Country code = Nigeria (NG); To Format = international format without spaces (E.164 or similar, e.g. +2348031234567).
3 · Action · Formatter by Zapier › Date/Time › Format (rename step "Clean date"): Input = [1. Delivery date]; To Format = YYYY-MM-DD; To Timezone = Africa/Lagos.

4 · Action · Google Sheets › Lookup Spreadsheet Row: Spreadsheet = your 0.4 workbook; Worksheet = Products; Lookup Column = name; Lookup Value = [1. Product]; tick the option to stop or flag the Zap if nothing is found. Returns the whole row (sku, price_ngn).
5 · Action · Formatter by Zapier › Utilities › Lookup Table: Lookup Key = [1. Area]; Lookup Table rows: Bodija = 1500, Mokola = 1500, Ring Road = 1500, Challenge = 2000; Fallback Value = 2500.
6 · Action · Formatter by Zapier › Numbers › Spreadsheet-Style Formula: Formula = [1. Quantity] * [4. price_ngn] + [5. Value] (e.g. 2 * 12500 + 1500 = 26500).
7 · Action · Formatter by Zapier › Numbers › Format Currency: Input = [6. Output]; Currency = NGN; Currency Locale = English (Nigeria) if listed. Output like ₦26,500.00, used only in the email.

8 · Action · Google Sheets › Create Spreadsheet Row: Spreadsheet = your 0.4 workbook; Worksheet = Orders; name = [1. Name]; phone = [2. Output]; delivery date = [3. Output]; sku = [4. sku]; unit price = [4. price_ngn]; quantity = [1. Quantity]; area = [1. Area]; delivery fee = [5. Value]; total = [6. Output] (the plain number); status = New.

9 · Action · Gmail › Send Email: To = Tolu's address (e.g. tolu@harvestlane.example); Subject = New order · [1. Name] · [3. Output] · [7. Output]; Body = each order field on its own line (name, phone from step 2, product, quantity, delivery date from step 3, area, fee from step 5, total from step 7).
setup: Multi-step Zaps need a paid Zapier plan or a trial of paid features.
Set your Zapier account time zone to Africa/Lagos (Settings) before building.
Add an Area dropdown (Bodija, Mokola, Ring Road, Challenge, …) to the order form from 1.1 Bronze.
Have the 0.4 workbook ready: a Products tab with headers name, sku, price_ngn in row 1, and an Orders tab with its header row in row 1.
Connect Google Forms, Google Sheets and Gmail with the Harvest Lane business Google account.
Build the nine steps in order, renaming each Formatter step (Clean phone, Clean date, Delivery fee, Total, Total for email) so the Zap reads like a recipe.
Test each step top to bottom, name the Zap HL · Form order → Sheet + alert, and Publish. Share it from the Zap's menu → Share to get the template link.
items.test: Submit a deliberately messy response: name "mrs ADEBAYO ", phone "0803 123 4567", product Tomatoes (crate), quantity 2, date 6 October, area Bodija. Orders gets a row with phone +2348031234567, date 2026-10-06, unit price 12500, fee 1500 and total 26500 (a number); Tolu's email subject ends with ₦26,500.00. A second order from an unlisted area (e.g. Apete) gets fee 2500.
items.tasks: About three tasks per order: the two Google Sheets steps and the Gmail step count, while the five Formatter steps use no tasks (check Zapier's pricing page for exact counting on searches).

walk.title: Build it: the one-Zap order line
walk.sample: mrs ADEBAYO · 0803 123 4567 · 2 tomato crates · 6 October · Bodija

steps.say: The order form is our trigger. Test it with deliberately messy data, so you can prove every cleaning step works.
First station: clean the phone number into one international format the riders' dialler understands.
Next we clean the date into the format we store, in Lagos time, so nothing is an hour off.
Prices change, so we look them up in the Products sheet Tolu controls. If the product isn't found, the Zap stops instead of pricing it at nothing.
Delivery fee comes from a small lookup table. The fallback charges a safe default for any new area, so the fee is never blank.
Now the maths: quantity times price, plus the fee.
We make a naira version of the total, but only for the email a person reads.
Save the clean row. Map the cleaned phone and date, and store the plain number total so the sheet can add it up.
Finally, tell Tolu with a readable summary. Test every step, name the Zap, and publish.
show: Subject: New order · name · date · total

walk.end: Nine steps, one Zap, about three tasks. Build it yourself, then check three totals by hand.
